India spends over ₹2 lakh crores on roads every year, yet most of them start crumbling within months. Potholes alone kill over 2,000 people annually. Meanwhile, other nations have roads that last 40 years with the same monsoons and heatwaves we blame for ours. This video breaks down why Indian roads fail so fast: from the engineering we ignore to the tender system that rewards bad work and exposes the cartels, corruption, and whistleblower silencing that keeps the rot in place. We also look at how other countries facing similar issues broke their own road mafias and built systems that actually work.

If they could fix it with similar conditions and worse starting points… why can’t we? Let’s understand the science, the money, the mafias, and what it would actuall
